title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
layout_note: One row of five boxes: input dataset, three numbered steps, output dataset. Under every box a column of worked-example text continues the same example (two candidate tool calls tracked through all steps), so the figure reads as a pipeline row over a table of its data.
grouping: The three processing steps sit on one light-grey background band that runs to the bottom of the figure, separating them from the input and output datasets at both ends, which stay on white. Datasets are pink-mauve boxes with italic labels; steps are light-blue boxes with a bold step number on its own line above the step name.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles without outlines, no shadows. Grey arrows connect the datasets to the band, blue arrows connect the steps inside it. The example text below is typeset math and plain sans-serif: bold x for text spans, c_i superscript 1 and 2 for the candidate calls, r_i for their results. The filtering criterion is written as an inequality on a tinted strip: green for the call that is kept (with a green '<'), pink-red for the call that is dropped (red '>'). The output example shows the inserted tool call inline as bold magenta bracketed text.
proposed_highlight: The method's steps are the only blue boxes and share the grey band; the result of the method, the inserted tool call, is the only bold magenta text in the output, and the keep/drop decision is carried by green versus red tint.
lesson: Run one concrete example under each pipeline stage in aligned columns, and show the keep-or-drop decision by tinting the kept candidate green and the rejected one red, so the tool-call insertion can be read off the bottom row.
notes: elements 'other' = the green/red tinted strips behind the inequality lines and the bracketed inline tool-call syntax. Venue NeurIPS from semantic-scholar; year 2023 is the arXiv year and the recorded venue year.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: self-supervised tool-use data generation for LMs
taxonomy.note: training 'other': self-supervised filtering of API calls by LM loss reduction, then finetuning on the augmented dataset

core.what: one row of five headers read left to right - pink LM Dataset, three numbered blue steps (Sample, Execute, Filter API Calls) on a grey band, pink LM Dataset with API Calls - with a worked example written under each header, so the example flows through the steps in columns

relations.form: header boxes joined by short straight arrows (grey into and out of the band, blue between steps), and each step's example text placed directly beneath its header
two candidate calls c_i^1 and c_i^2 run as two aligned rows across the columns: question, then executed result (Steel City, United States), then the filter verdict
under Filter API Calls each candidate's loss with its result is set against the minimum of the two baselines, highlighted green with '<' for the kept call and red with '>' for the rejected one

the input text x is split into prefix 'Pittsburgh is also known as' and continuation 'the Steel City', and the output x* re-joins them with the kept call '[QA(What ...? -> Steel City)]' inserted in magenta

channels.colour: pink = datasets (and the inserted API call in the output text, the new dataset content); blue = the three pipeline steps; green highlight = call kept, red highlight = call rejected - one meaning each
channels.shape: rounded rectangles only; the content is text, with losses typeset as expressions
channels.line: grey arrows = data in and out of the pipeline; blue arrows = step to step
channels.frame: a light grey band behind the three steps = the annotation pipeline

quality.strengths: the data are drawn as data: one real sentence is carried through every step with two candidate calls in aligned rows, so the reader sees what is sampled, what comes back and why one is kept; the green/red highlight with '<' and '>' makes the filter's decision readable without the formula; the step boxes form one straight row with the pipeline band marking the new part
quality.weaknesses: the filter criterion is shown as typeset loss expressions L_i(...) and min(...), which the reader must parse to see what is compared; the model that does the sampling and scoring is never drawn; the rejected call's row simply ends, with no mark of it being dropped in the output column

insights.structure: One row of five rounded boxes, mauve 'LM Dataset' at each end and three numbered light-blue steps (Sample, Execute, Filter API Calls) sitting together on a grey band that runs down to the figure bottom.
insights.data: Under every box a column continues one worked example: the Pittsburgh text spans x, two candidate calls c_i^1 and c_i^2 as questions, their results r_i, and the filter inequalities on tinted strips (green with '<' kept, pink with '>' dropped).
insights.emphasis: The kept/dropped decision is colour-coded green vs pink-red and carried into the output, where the inserted call '[QA(What ...? -> Steel City)]' appears in bold magenta inline in the sentence.
insights.flow: Strictly left to right: grey arrows from and to the dataset boxes, blue arrows between the steps; the example text is read top to bottom inside each column.
insights.avoid: The two candidate calls are tracked only by row position and superscripts; nothing marks that the dropped c_i^2 is discarded before the output column.

arrangement.units: one row of pipeline boxes; the three processing steps are grouped on a grey background band, each step heading a column of example text
arrangement.inputs_as: a dataset box plus quoted example text beneath it
arrangement.losses_at: filter criterion written as inequalities under step 3
